papers.title_en: Cinematize from Unreal: Agentic Choreography for Controllable World Simulation
papers.authors: Zifan Song, Caihua Shan, Kaitao Song, Yifan Yang, Dongsheng Li, Cairong Zhao
papers.evidence: 基于智能体的语言驱动世界编排，在虚幻引擎中保持持久状态与可控动态
papers.tldr: 可控世界模拟不仅需要视觉合理，还要保持持久状态、协调动作和可编辑时间结构。CineU把Unreal工程视为可检查的世界表示，让智能体生成可执行代码，并融合分层编排、资产检索与几何约束放置、代码合成及多阶段验证修复。实验表明，该系统在场景构建、选择性编辑和多镜头电影编排中提升任务完成度与局部恢复能力。这显示可执行世界状态能补充学习式视觉生成，支撑可控且可修订的模拟世界。
papers.abstract_en: Controllable world simulation requires more than visually plausible frames: scenes must retain persistent state, coordinated actions, and editable temporal structure. Generative world models offer flexible visual synthesis, but their outputs do not always expose the objects and transitions needed for precise revision. Graphics engines provide executable state and direct control, yet translating language into valid operations requires specialized knowledge of assets, geometry, and interdependent APIs. We present CineU (Cinematize from Unreal), an agentic system for language-driven world orchestration and cinematic choreography within Unreal Engine. From a code-based world modeling perspective, an Unreal project serves as a persistent, inspectable world representation, while agent-generated code specifies operations whose effects can be executed and verified. CineU combines hierarchical orchestration, cascaded asset retrieval and geometry-constrained placement, capability-aligned code synthesis, and multi-stage verification with localized repair. Shared scene and timeline context coordinates entities, actions, camera trajectories, and shot boundaries while supporting dependency-aware revisions. Experiments on scene construction, selective editing, multi-shot cinematography, and component ablations show how specialized execution knowledge and engine feedback improve task completion and targeted recovery. CineU illustrates how executable world state can complement learned visual generation to support controllable and revisable simulated worlds.
